newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF sale to be private placement -paper.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF sale to be private placement -paper.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe is set to announce that the sale of the state's stake in defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF will take place through a private placement, the newspaper Le Monde said on Monday.

"Juppe seems determined that it will be a procedure for a private placement. He could announce it this week, in any case before the end of the month," the afternoon daily said in its Monday edition dated February 18.
The Prime Minister's office declined comment on the newspaper report.
Another option for the government would be to privatise the state's 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF through a market float.
On Thursday, Juppe held a series of meetings with the Finance and Industry Ministers and a representative of the Defence Minister.

He also spoke with the chairman of Thomson SA and Thomson-CSF, Marcel Roulet, and with Serge Tchuruk of Alcatel Alsthom and Jean-Luc Lagardere of Lagardere Groupe, who are interested in acquiring Thomson-CSF.
Thomson SA, wholly owned by the state, is the 58 percent parent of Thomson-CSF.
After the meeting, Juppe's office said a decision on the procedure for the sale would be made before the end of February.

Le Monde said on Monday that Juppe had tried to get a joint offer from Alcatel and Lagardere's Matra unit but did not succeed. It said Thomson's Roulet favoured a float, because this would leave the company with the biggest margin of manoeuvre.

Defence Minister Charles Millon and Finance Minister Jean Arthuis were said to favour a private placement -- Millon because it would allow the government to steer the restructuring of the defence sector and Arthuis because he believes that would raise more money for the state.
The government stated its preference in October for an offer from Lagardere for Thomson SA, which also owns consumer electronics firm Thomson Multimedia, over a rival bid from Alcatel.
Lagardere had teamed up with South Korea's Daewoo Electronics but the government cancelled the procedure in December after the independent Privatisation Commission said it could not approve the deal.
The sales of the Thomson-CSF stake and TMM will now be conducted separately.
Alcatel has boosted its position by lining up Aerospatiale and Dassault Aviation for a joint bid.
Last week, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA) chief executive Manfred Bischoff said the outcome of the Thomson-CSF privatisation was of crucial importance to the future of Germany's defence industry.
Shares in Alcatel were 2.21 percent higher at 600 francs at 1339 GMT, Lagardere was up 0.36 percent at 167 francs and Thomson-CSF was up 0.58 percent at 173 francs.
